entities.summary: Frank Lloyd Wright Sr. was an American architect, designer, writer, and educator. He designed more than 1,000 structures over a creative period of 70 years. Wright played a key role in the architectural movements of the twentieth century, influencing architects worldwide through his works and mentoring hundreds of apprentices in his Taliesin Fellowship. Wright believed in designing in harmony with humanity and the environment, a philosophy he called organic architecture. This philosophy was exemplified in Fallingwater (1935), which has been called "the best all-time work of American architecture".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Frank Lloyd Wright's organic architecture philosophy and designs had a profound impact on modern architecture, influencing architects worldwide and shaping the development of sustainable and environmentally conscious building practices. His work continues to inspire generations of architects and designers.
